lesson.title: Blanks, repeats and impossible values
lesson.subtitle: What a blank means, repeats, impossible values, and a Python check

video.title: Blanks, repeats and impossible values
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — the science teacher, runs the weather club (main character)

chapters.label: A flood on a sunny day
A blank is not a zero

scenes.visual: Icon cards: A flood?; A sunny day; 999: “broken”. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our weather club's chart showed a flood on Tuesday. It was the sunniest day of the week! One gauge had sent nine nine nine: its code for “I'm broken”.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: blanks, repeats and impossible values, and how to catch them.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: 25 out of 20; 999 mm in a day; Minus 4 pupils; Check, don't average.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some values are impossible. A mark of twenty-five out of twenty. Rain of nine hundred and ninety-nine millimetres in a day. Minus four pupils. They need checking, not averaging.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “0” (Measured: none) and “Blank” (Not measured; Blank → 0: a lie).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A blank is not a zero
scenes.narration: A blank is not a zero. Zero means we measured, and there was none. Blank means nobody measured. If you turn blanks into zeros, your average becomes a lie.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: One reading, sent twice; Same station, same day? Remove one.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Repeats are the same thing counted twice: one reading, sent two times. Remove the copy, but only when it's really the same station, on the same day.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A rain gauge reading is blank. What should you write in your report?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Zero: not a fact; Average: a guess; Say it's missing.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: That one reading is missing. Zero would be a fact you don't have, and the average would be a guess. Say what's missing, and find out why.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: marks = [14, "", 9, 25, ""] … Caption: Prints 2: two marks are missing
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Python can check every value. Loop through the marks, and count the blanks. Then flag any mark below zero or above twenty.

scenes.visual: Numbered steps: In range: 0 to 20; Not empty; No repeats; Failed? Set aside, ask.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A check is a rule the data must pass. In range: zero to twenty. Not empty. No repeats. When a check fails, set the row aside and ask; don't delete it.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: 4 clubs; Checks one by one; All off: 6 stations!.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, four weather clubs send rain readings. Turn on the checks one by one, and watch the rainfall report change. Turn them all off: suddenly there are six stations!

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A mark says twenty-five, but the test was out of twenty. What do you do?

scenes.visual: Summary card: A blank is not a zero; Find repeats; Catch impossible values; Ask; don't guess. Takeaway bar: Clean data is honest about what's missing.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Check it with the teacher: twenty-five out of twenty can't happen. Remember: a blank is not a zero. Look for repeats and impossible values. And when something's wrong, ask; don't guess.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A table you made; Circle each problem; Write what you'd do. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: check a table you made, or one from class. Circle every blank, every repeat and every impossible value. For each one, write what you'd do.

checkpoints.prompt: A rain gauge reading is blank. What should you write in your report?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — say it's missing. Zero would be a fact you don't have, and an average would be a guess.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — nobody measured, so you don't know it was zero, and an average is only a guess. Say it's missing.

checkpoints.prompt: A mark says 25, but the test was out of 20. What do you do?

options.text: Keep it: the pupil did very well
Check it with the teacher: it's impossible

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a mark can't be above the maximum, so someone made a mistake. Ask, don't guess.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — 25 out of 20 is impossible, and changing it to 20 is a guess. Check it with the teacher.
